response: Assessment of carotid artery stenosis before coronary artery bypass surgery is not always necessary. Selective screening of patients can be an effective approach, particularly for those aged over 70 years, with carotid bruit, a history of cerebrovascular disease, diabetes mellitus, or peripheral vascular disease (PVD). This selective approach can reduce the screening load by approximately 40% without significantly impacting surgical management or neurological outcomes. Therefore, a universal assessment of carotid artery stenosis before coronary artery bypass surgery may not be required, and a more targeted approach based on patient risk factors can be considered.
